8947.e: A spring stores force when it is squeezed. When you let go, it releases the force again and springs back.
8947.m: Springs store force and give it back.

8948.q: How do migrating geese often take turns when flying in a V formation?
a: The lead bird at the front changes regularly
Only one single goose ever flies at the front
No goose ever flies at the front
They only ever fly in circles
8948.e: The goose at the front faces the most air resistance and gets tired quickly. That is why the geese take turns, so that none of them gets too exhausted.
8948.m: The lead birds take turns when flying.

8949.q: Roughly how long is an adult red kite from beak to tail tip?
8949.e: With a body length of around 60 to 70 centimetres, the red kite is one of Europe's medium-sized birds of prey. Even so, it looks very large in the sky because of its long wings.
8949.m: The red kite is about 65 cm long.

8950.q: What sound does an elephant often make with its trunk?
8950.e: When elephants are excited or angry, they give a loud trumpeting call through their trunk. You can hear this sound from far away.

8951.q: Which sense especially helps the eel to find food at night?
8951.e: Eels have an excellent sense of smell. With it they find prey even in the dark and in murky water.
8951.m: Eels find prey with their nose.

8952.q: What is special about reindeer antlers?
a: Both males and females have them
8952.e: In reindeer, both bulls and cows have antlers. In all other deer species, only the males have them.
8952.m: Both males and females have antlers.

8953.q: Which senses are especially well developed in the stone marten?
a: Only feeling in the tips of its ears
8953.e: When hunting at night, stone martens rely mainly on their good hearing and their keen sense of smell. This way they find prey even in the dark.
8953.m: Nose and ears guide the stone marten at night.

8954.q: Roughly how many eggs can a female perch lay?
8954.e: Female perch lay a great many eggs, often several tens of thousands. But only a small number of them become adult fish.
8954.m: Perch lay a great many eggs.

8955.q: Why is the orca seen as a very clever animal?
a: Because it learns clever hunting tactics and communicates with others
8955.e: Orcas learn from each other and plan their hunts together. That is why researchers think they are very intelligent.

a: A group of countries that share the French language
8956.e: La Francophonie links countries and regions where French is spoken, including French-speaking Switzerland. It promotes culture and cooperation.

8957.q: What happens shortly before a butterfly comes out of its pupa?
8957.e: Shortly before it hatches, you can already see the colours of the wings through the thinning case. Then it will not be long until it comes out.
8957.m: The case becomes see-through before hatching.

8958.q: Which country is often called “Europe’s last dictatorship”?
8958.e: Belarus under Alexander Lukashenko is often called “Europe’s last dictatorship”. Elections there are not considered free and fair, and critics are persecuted.
8958.m: Belarus is seen as Europe’s last dictatorship.

8959.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult male puma get?
8959.e: Males are usually heavier than females. They often weigh between 60 and 100 kilograms.
8959.m: Pumas weigh about as much as a person.

8960.q: What is a large group of sheep called?
8960.e: Lots of sheep together are called a flock. Sheep like to stay in a group because they feel safer that way.
8960.m: Lots of sheep make up a flock.

8961.q: How many young does a female orangutan usually have at once?
8961.e: Usually only one baby is born. Twins are very rare.
8961.m: Usually only one baby is born.

8962.q: Why are wetlands so important for the white stork?
a: there it finds lots of frogs and insects
there are fewer other birds there
it is warmer there than elsewhere
8962.e: In wetlands such as marshes and damp meadows there is lots of food for the stork. That is why these places are very important for it.
8962.m: Wetlands offer plenty of food for storks.

8963.q: How long does an adult mosquito usually live?
8963.e: An adult mosquito usually lives for only a few weeks. But some females survive the winter hidden in a cellar.
8963.m: Mosquitoes only live a few weeks.

8964.q: How are okapis usually kept in zoos?
a: On their own, with lots of space and places to retreat to
In large herds in a small space
8964.e: Okapis live alone and need peace and quiet. That is why zoos usually keep them on their own in large enclosures with hiding places.

a: Yes, many species can, especially the males
8965.e: Males are lighter and often fly better. The females of some species are too heavy and can only flutter at most.

8966.q: What does the common wall lizard usually do in cool, cloudy weather?
a: It tends to stay hidden and is not very active
It becomes especially fast and active
8966.e: Without the warmth of the sun, the wall lizard lacks the energy for quick movements. So on days like that it prefers to hide.

8967.q: How do giraffes warn each other of danger?
a: They watch each other and run away together
They change the colour of their coat
They lie flat in the grass
8967.e: When a giraffe suddenly becomes alert or runs away, other giraffes nearby notice too. In this way a warning spreads quickly through the whole group.
8967.m: Giraffes warn each other by watching.

8968.q: Compared with many other pets, what is noticeable about how guinea pigs hide illness?
a: They often only show pain very late
They show pain very clearly straight away
They become loud when in pain
8968.e: As prey animals, guinea pigs in the wild try to hide weakness so that enemies do not see them as easy prey. That is why you often only notice illness in them late.
8968.m: Guinea pigs hide illness for a long time.

8969.q: What do tigers have on the backs of their ears that they use to communicate?
8969.e: Tigers have white spots on the backs of their ears. These help tiger cubs to follow their mother through tall grass.
8969.m: White ear spots help the cubs follow.

8970.q: Which animals are among the enemies of the grass snake?
8970.e: Birds of prey, storks, foxes and martens catch grass snakes. Pet cats are also a danger.
8970.m: Birds of prey and foxes hunt grass snakes.

8973.q: What does the beak of shanks, a group of wading birds, usually look like?
a: Wide and flat like a duck's
8973.e: With their slender beak they look for food in mud and shallow water. It can also grip small animals well.
8973.m: A long, slender beak for probing.

8974.q: What danger does the decline in flying insects pose for common swifts?
a: less food, which can reduce breeding success
it makes them too heavy to fly
it makes them die earlier than usual
it makes them lose the ability to fly completely
8974.e: Because swifts feed almost only on flying insects, the worldwide decline in insects affects them directly. Less food can mean that fewer young birds survive.

8975.q: How fast does a young pike grow?
a: Quite fast in its first year
It does not grow at all in its life
Only a little every ten years
It only gets bigger in winter
8975.e: Young pike grow quite fast in their first year. The more food they find, the faster they grow.

8976.q: How can you often tell that a goldfish is not well?
a: It swims strangely or lies still on the bottom
It jumps out of the water for joy
8976.e: Sick goldfish often swim in an unusual way or lie still on the bottom or at the surface. This is a sign that they need help.
8976.m: Unusual swimming is a sign of illness.

8977.q: Which body parts do millipedes and centipedes have that insects do not have in this form?
a: Many similar body segments with legs
A hard shell like a mussel's
8977.e: The body of millipedes and centipedes is made of many similar segments with legs. Insects are divided into head, thorax and abdomen.
8977.m: Many similar segments shape the body.

8978.q: How does the mother stone marten raise her young?
a: Alone in a sheltered hiding place
In an open field with no hiding place
8978.e: The mother gives birth to her young in a well-sheltered hiding place and looks after them there on her own. Only after a few months do the young become independent.
8978.m: The mother raises her young alone, in safety.

8980.q: Where does the name ‘white rhinoceros’ probably really come from?
a: From a word for ‘wide’ that was wrongly translated
From the white colour of its horn
Because it turns white in winter
Because it lives in the snow
8980.e: It is thought that a word meaning ‘wide’ was wrongly turned into ‘white’ in English. That is how the name ‘white rhinoceros’ came about, even though it is not white at all.
8980.m: White probably comes from wide, not from the colour.

8981.q: How many mute swan cygnets usually hatch from one clutch?
8981.e: From the five to eight eggs, usually just as many cygnets hatch. But not all of them always survive.
8981.m: Usually five to eight cygnets hatch.

8982.q: How can the snow leopard also use its coat to help it?
a: To hide from prey among the rocks
8982.e: The grey colour and the spots make it blend in with the rock. This lets it get close to its prey.

8983.q: What is it called when wool is made into a thread before you knit something with it?
8983.e: The sheared wool is first spun into a thread before you can knit a jumper from it, for example. In the past, this was often done by hand on a spinning wheel.

8984.q: What does a dog use to smell much better than a person?
8984.e: A dog's nose is incredibly sensitive. It can tell apart a thousand times more smells than a human nose.
8984.m: A dog's nose smells much better.

8985.q: What especially sets a wolf's teeth apart from those of plant-eating animals?
a: Long, sharp fangs for tearing meat
Wide grinding teeth for grinding grass
Missing teeth in the upper jaw
Teeth that keep growing like a rodent's
8985.e: As a meat eater, the wolf has strong, pointed fangs that it uses to grab prey and tear the meat. Plant eaters, on the other hand, have wide grinding teeth.

8987.q: What does a trout like to eat most?
a: Only fish food from a packet
8987.e: Trout mainly eat small insects, worms and other small animals in the water. Sometimes they also snap up insects from the surface of the water.

8988.q: What does the tiger need its long tail for?
8988.e: The long tail helps the tiger keep its balance when running and jumping. It works like a rudder.

8989.q: How fast can an African wild dog run for a short time?
8989.e: Over short distances, wild dogs can reach around 60 km/h. On top of that, they have great stamina.
8989.m: Fast and with lots of stamina.

8990.q: What does a seahorse's mouth look like?
a: Like a round suction cup with no opening
8990.e: The mouth is tube-shaped and points forwards. The seahorse uses it to suck in its prey, as if through a straw.
8990.m: The mouth is a thin tube.

8991.q: What happens when a strange marten enters another marten's territory?
a: There may be quarrels and fights
They immediately share the territory peacefully
The stranger becomes the pack leader
Nothing, martens do not have territories
8991.e: Martens often stay loyal to their territory and do not like other martens in their area. If two martens meet, there may be threatening displays or fights.

8992.q: What colour is the drake mallard's beak usually?
8992.e: The male's beak is usually yellowish. The female's is more orange-brown with dark spots.

a: Some species have spots that sense light
All jellyfish have two large eyes
Jellyfish have eyes like a cat
8993.e: Some kinds of jellyfish have small spots they can use to tell light from dark. But they do not have real eyes like us humans.

8994.q: What do meerkats have on their belly that helps them sunbathe?
a: A layer of fat like seals
8994.e: The fur on their belly is thin and the skin is dark. This lets them soak up the warmth of the sun well.
8994.m: The dark belly soaks up the sun's warmth.

8995.q: The scientific name of the ibex is Capra ibex. What does the Latin word Capra mean?
8995.e: Capra means goat in Latin. So the ibex belongs to the same genus as the domestic goat.

8996.q: What is one difference between a grass snake and a slow worm?
a: The grass snake is a true snake, the slow worm is a legless lizard
The slow worm is more venomous
8996.e: The slow worm looks like a snake, but it is a lizard. It has eyelids that move.
8996.m: The slow worm is a lizard, not a snake.

8997.q: How do horses usually sleep without falling over?
8997.e: Horses can sleep standing up because their legs can lock in place. But for deep sleep they sometimes lie down.

8999.q: How long does a gibbon mother usually feed her baby with milk?
8999.e: Young gibbons drink their mother's milk for a long time. They stay with the family for many years until they are independent.
8999.m: Young gibbons drink their mother's milk for a long time.

9000.q: Why is the common wall lizard protected in Switzerland?
a: Because its habitat keeps shrinking due to building
Because it is very popular as a pet
9000.e: Stony, warm habitats are being lost to building projects. That is why the common wall lizard is protected in Switzerland.
9000.m: Protected because its habitats are disappearing.

9001.q: What does the water louse mainly eat?
9001.e: The water louse eats dead leaves and other remains. In this way it helps to break things down in the water.

9003.q: Why should you not wake a hamster suddenly?
a: It could get a fright and bite
9003.e: Hamsters are easily startled when they are disturbed in their sleep. So it is better to wake them gently and carefully.

9004.q: What is EFTA, which Switzerland also belongs to?
a: A free trade association of European states outside the EU
9004.e: EFTA (the European Free Trade Association) links countries such as Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, which do not belong to the EU but still want to make trade easier.
9004.m: EFTA promotes free trade outside the EU.

9005.q: What are the thick, hard hairs of the wild boar called?
9005.e: The wild boar's coat is made of hard, thick hairs. They are called bristles. They protect against cold and thorns.

9006.q: What is the lake trout's swim bladder for?
a: It helps it float in the water
9006.e: The gas-filled bladder balances buoyancy. This lets the fish float at one depth without using much energy.

9007.q: How is the mountain gorilla's fur different from a lowland gorilla's?
a: It is thicker and longer, because it is colder in the mountains
It is much shorter and thinner
There is no difference at all
9007.e: In the cool mountains, mountain gorillas need thicker fur to stay warm. Lowland gorillas live in warmer places and have shorter fur.
9007.m: Mountain gorillas have thicker, warmer fur.

9008.q: Where does a gorilla usually build its sleeping nest?
a: On the ground or sometimes in trees
9008.e: Big gorillas, especially the males, usually sleep on the ground. Smaller and lighter animals sometimes build their nest in trees.
9008.m: Gorillas sleep on the ground or in trees.

9009.q: What do bull moose do with their antlers in the rut?
a: They fight each other with them
9009.e: The bulls test their strength in fights. The stronger animal has a better chance with the cows.

9010.q: What shows that dolphins are very clever animals?
a: They recognise themselves in a mirror
They build nests out of branches
9010.e: Dolphins pass what is called the mirror test. This means they recognise their own reflection, which only a few animals can do.
9010.m: Dolphins recognise themselves in a mirror.

9011.e: Young grasshoppers are called nymphs. They already look like small adult grasshoppers.

a: Not at all, not even a metre
9012.e: Chickens can flutter and fly up for a short time, for example onto a fence. But their wings are too weak for long flights.

9013.q: Roughly how big does a blackbird get?
9013.e: An adult blackbird is about 24 to 25 centimetres long. That is about as long as a ruler.
9013.m: A blackbird is around 25 cm long.

9014.q: How does the wels catfish mainly move?
a: It wriggles with its body and its long anal fin
It flies short distances over the water
It rolls itself up and tumbles along
9014.e: The wels catfish swims with wave-like movements. Its very long anal fin helps it do this.
9014.m: The wels catfish swims in waves.

9015.q: When is the Alpine salamander mainly active?
a: In damp weather, often after rain
Only in the depths of winter
9015.e: The Alpine salamander loves damp conditions and comes out of its hiding places especially after rain or in damp weather. It avoids dry weather.
9015.m: It is seen most after rain.

9016.q: Which subspecies of brown bear is known for being especially big and lives in Russia?
9016.e: The Kamchatka brown bear is one of the largest brown bear subspecies and lives on the Russian peninsula of Kamchatka. It can be much heavier than the European brown bear.
9016.m: Kamchatka bears are among the biggest brown bears.

9017.q: Is the Javan rhinoceros a very rare kind of rhino?
a: Yes, it is one of the rarest animals in the world
No, there are very many of them
No, it is not threatened at all
9017.e: The Javan rhinoceros is extremely rare today. Only very few animals are left, in a national park in Indonesia.
9017.m: The Javan rhino has become very rare.

9018.q: What is one important reason why packs of wild dogs go on the move?
9018.e: Wild dogs follow their prey animals and look for new hunting grounds. Only while raising their pups do they stay at the den for longer.

9019.q: In which season does the carrion crow typically breed in Switzerland?
a: in spring, usually March and April
9019.e: In Switzerland, carrion crows usually start breeding in March or April. This gives the young birds enough time to become independent before winter.

9020.q: Roughly how fast can a galloping horse go?
a: Up to about 60 kilometres per hour
Up to about 5 kilometres per hour
Up to about 300 kilometres per hour
Horses cannot go faster than walking
9020.e: At a gallop, horses can reach impressive speeds of up to 60 kilometres per hour. That is faster than an everyday bike ride.
9020.m: Horses gallop at up to 60 km/h.

9021.q: What do male stag beetles mainly use their ‘antlers’ for?
9021.e: The males wrestle over females and try to throw their rival off the branch. Usually not much harm is done.
9021.m: Males use their antlers to fight over females.

9022.q: What happens to most bumblebees in autumn?
a: They die, only young queens survive
They all sleep together in the nest
They all spend the winter in the beehive
9022.e: At the end of summer, almost all the bumblebees in a colony die. Only the young queens survive the winter and start a new colony in spring.
9022.m: Only young queens survive the winter.

9023.q: Why does a wasp sometimes sting?
a: To protect itself or its nest
To lay eggs in the skin
9023.e: A wasp only stings when it is afraid or defending its nest. Otherwise it usually leaves you alone.
9023.m: Wasps only sting to defend themselves.

9024.q: What is the largest rodent in Europe?
9024.e: Including its tail, the beaver can grow more than a metre long. With its sharp front teeth it can even fell thick tree trunks.
9024.m: The beaver is Europe's largest rodent.

9025.q: How do ring-tailed lemurs mainly move about in trees?
a: They climb and jump from branch to branch
They swing on long vines like gibbons
They glide with flaps of skin
9025.e: Ring-tailed lemurs are good climbers and jump safely between branches. Their long tail helps them keep their balance.
9025.m: Ring-tailed lemurs climb and jump skilfully.

9026.q: How many golden stars are on the flag of the European Union?
9026.e: The EU flag shows twelve golden stars in a circle on a blue background, regardless of the number of member states. Twelve stands for completeness and unity.
9026.m: The EU flag always has 12 stars.

9027.q: Which Swiss butterfly is bright yellow?
9027.e: The brimstone has a strong yellow colour, especially the male. You often see it as early as the beginning of spring.

9028.q: Why are wood ants useful for the forest?
a: They eat all the healthy trees
They drive away all the birds
9028.e: Wood ants hunt many small pests that could harm trees. That is why they are also called the health police of the forest.

9029.q: What was the well-known small car from East Germany called?
9029.e: The Trabant was a simple car built in East Germany. Many people had to wait a long time to get one.
9029.m: The Trabant was the car of East Germany.

9030.q: What does loud teeth chattering in a guinea pig often mean?
9030.e: Teeth chattering can be a sign that a guinea pig feels unwell or is stressed. You should then look closely at what is wrong.
9030.m: Teeth chattering can mean it feels unwell.

9032.q: How did the red salmon get its name?
a: It turns bright red when it spawns
It lives in red coral reefs
It has red scales from birth
9032.e: The red salmon, also called sockeye, is silvery in the sea. When it swims up rivers to spawn, its body turns bright red.
9032.m: The red salmon turns red when it spawns.

9033.q: Why can cockchafers fly despite their heavy body?
a: They beat their hind wings strongly
They have balloons in their body
They use their wing cases as propellers
9033.e: The hind wings unfold from under the wing cases and beat quickly. Meanwhile the wing cases are held spread out to the sides.
9033.m: The hind wings carry the beetle.

9034.e: Drones are the males in a bee colony. Their main job is to mate with a young queen.

9035.q: What is the striped and spotted coat of young tapirs for?
9035.e: Light and shade in the forest make the stripes and spots blend in with the surroundings. After a few months the pattern disappears.
9035.m: The spotted coat camouflages young tapirs.

9036.q: Why are bogs important for the climate?
a: They store large amounts of carbon in the ground
They make oxygen faster than forests
They cool the Earth strongly through evaporation
They stop rain in the surrounding area
9036.e: Bogs are made of dead plant remains that hardly break down under water. As a result a lot of carbon stays locked in the ground instead of entering the air as CO2.
9036.m: Bogs store a lot of carbon in the ground.

9037.q: Why do bonobo populations recover only slowly?
a: Because females only have a baby every few years
Because they have ten babies every year
Because they only have babies in zoos
Because the young are independent straight away
9037.e: Bonobos have a long pregnancy and raise their young for a long time. That is why a population only grows slowly.

9038.q: What shape is an eel's body?
9038.e: The eel has a long, stretched-out, almost round body. This helps it squeeze into narrow cracks.

9039.q: Does the magpie move to warmer areas in winter?
a: No, it stays in its territory all year round
9039.e: The magpie is a resident bird and does not leave its territory even in winter. It finds enough food even in the cold season.

9040.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult stoat get?
9040.e: An adult stoat usually weighs only between 100 and 300 grams. Males weigh a little more than females.
9040.m: A stoat weighs only a few hundred grams.

9041.q: Which sense is also well developed in hyenas?
a: A magnetic sense like migrating birds
9041.e: Hyenas hear well and recognise the calls of other hyenas from far away. Their hearing also helps them look for prey.

9042.q: How many pups can a female African wild dog have in one litter?
9042.e: Wild dogs have large litters, often with ten or more pups. That is more than most other members of the dog family.

9043.q: What does electrical resistance in ohms tell you?
a: How much a material hinders the flow of electricity
How much light a material lets through
9043.e: A high resistance means that a material strongly hinders the flow of electricity; a low resistance lets electricity flow easily. Metals such as copper have a very low resistance and therefore conduct well.
9043.m: Resistance slows down the flow of electricity.

9044.q: On which continent does the spotted hyena live?
a: In Africa south of the Sahara
9044.e: Spotted hyenas live in the savannahs and semi-deserts of Africa south of the Sahara. Today there are no longer any wild ones in Europe.

9045.q: Where does the name ‘stone marten’ probably come from?
a: From its liking for rocks and stony areas
Because it comes from a place called Stone
9045.e: The name stone marten points to the animal's liking for rocky and stony habitats. In towns and villages, too, it likes to use walls and piles of stones.
9045.m: Stony areas gave the stone marten its name.

9046.q: What do whitefish use to breathe underwater?
9046.e: The gills take in the oxygen dissolved in the water. That is why whitefish depend on water rich in oxygen.

9047.q: What does a badger do when its sett becomes too small over time?
a: It digs extra tunnels and chambers
It builds a nest in the trees
It moves into the water for ever
It builds a nest of stones above ground
9047.e: Badger setts are often extended over many generations. Over time this creates a huge system of tunnels.
9047.m: Badger setts grow over many years.

9048.q: Which family does the tawny owl belong to?
9048.e: The tawny owl belongs to the family of typical owls, also called Strigidae. This family includes most owl species worldwide.
9048.m: The tawny owl is one of the typical owls.

9050.q: What kind of skeleton do cockchafers have?
a: An outer skeleton made of chitin
An inner skeleton made of bone
A skeleton of lime like snails
9050.e: The body is supported by armour made of chitin. It protects the beetle and keeps it in shape.
9050.m: The armour is made of chitin.

9051.q: What is the capital of Switzerland?
9051.e: Switzerland's government and parliament work in Bern. Many important decisions are made there.
9051.m: Bern is the capital of Switzerland.

9078.q: What do you have fingernails for?
9078.e: Nails are made of a hard material called keratin. They protect the sensitive skin at the fingertips.

9083.q: What does the presence of brown trout tell you about a stream?
a: The water is clean and rich in oxygen
The water is full of mud
9083.e: The brown trout needs very good water quality. That is why it shows that a stream is healthy.
9083.m: Trout are a sign of clean water.

9105.q: Who was an important communist leader in Vietnam?
9105.e: Ho Chi Minh fought for an independent, communist Vietnam. The city of Saigon was later named after him.
9105.m: Ho Chi Minh led the communists in Vietnam.

9106.q: Which country has a red and blue Taegeuk symbol, similar to yin and yang, in the centre of its flag?
9106.e: The South Korean flag shows the red and blue Taegeuk symbol in the middle, which stands for harmony. Four black trigrams are arranged around it.
9106.m: South Korea shows the Taegeuk symbol.

9143.q: Which vitamin does your body make in the skin with the help of sunlight?
9143.e: When sunlight falls on the skin, the body makes vitamin D. It is important for strong bones.

9168.q: Who composed the famous song “The Trout” (“Die Forelle”)?
9168.e: In 1817 Franz Schubert set to music a poem about a trout in a stream. Later he also wrote the “Trout Quintet”.

a: A group that collects signatures to put a law to the people
A committee of the Federal Council
A department of the Federal Chancellery
9220.e: If citizens do not agree with a new law, they can join together in a referendum committee. They then collect signatures for the optional referendum.
9220.m: Referendum committees collect signatures against laws.

a: China’s communist dictator, responsible for millions of deaths.
9236.e: Mao Zedong ruled China from 1949 to 1976. Programmes such as the “Great Leap Forward” and the “Cultural Revolution” cost millions of people their lives.
9236.m: Mao ruled China with a harsh hand.

9243.q: Why does a metal handle feel colder than a wooden handle, even though both are the same temperature?
a: Metal conducts heat away from your hand faster
Metal is always really colder than wood
Your skin is allergic to metal
9243.e: Metal is a good conductor of heat and draws the heat away from your hand quickly. Wood conducts heat badly, so it feels warmer, even though both objects are the same temperature.
9243.m: Good conductors of heat feel colder.

9254.q: Which animal family does the leopard in the picture belong to?
9254.e: The leopard is a predator from the cat family. Within it, it counts as one of the big cats.
9254.m: The leopard is a big cat.

9256.q: What does the Federal Council do?
9256.e: The Federal Council is made up of several people who run Switzerland together. They make important decisions for the whole country.

9260.q: Why do astronauts wear a special suit in space?
a: Because there is no air to breathe there
Because it always rains in space
Because it is very loud there
Because there is a lot of dust there
9260.e: In space there is no air and no oxygen. The spacesuit gives the astronauts air and protects them from cold and heat.
9260.m: In space there is no air to breathe.

9263.q: What is particularly harmful to brown trout in a stream?
a: Sewage and fertiliser, which use up oxygen
9263.e: Polluted water often contains less oxygen and also toxic substances. Trout cannot cope with that well.

9264.q: You rub a balloon on your jumper and hold it against the wall. What happens?
a: The balloon sticks to the wall
The balloon falls straight to the floor
9264.e: Rubbing gives the balloon an electric charge. This static electricity pulls it to the wall.
9264.m: Rubbing gives things an electric charge.

9268.q: What decides which blood group (A, B, AB or 0) a person has?
a: Certain markers on the surface of the red blood cells
9268.e: Certain proteins sit on red blood cells. Their combination decides the blood group.
9268.m: Blood groups come from proteins in the blood.

9283.q: What do ants use to see their surroundings?
9283.e: Ants have compound eyes made up of many tiny parts. With them they mainly see movement.

9284.q: What does the garden cross spider like to eat most?
a: Flying insects such as flies and wasps
9284.e: The garden cross spider feeds on insects that fly into its web. These include flies, midges and wasps.

9285.q: What is typical of gibbons’ arms?
a: They are very long compared with the body
They are shorter than the legs
They are joined by gliding membranes
They are thicker than the legs but very short
9285.e: The long arms help gibbons swing through the branches. They are clearly longer than the legs.
9285.m: Long arms are the gibbon’s trademark.

9286.q: What is a so-called food ball in the common swift?
a: a lump of many insects shaped into a ball with saliva
a round egg with an especially hard shell
a small stone in the nest
a pile of feathers for warmth
9286.e: During a hunting flight, swift parents collect many insects and use saliva to shape them into a compact food ball. They then bring it to the hungry chicks in the nest.
9286.m: Many insects are shaped into a food ball.

9287.q: What role does the pancreas play in the digestive system?
a: It produces digestive enzymes and hormones such as insulin
It stores fat for the winter
It filters the air you breathe
9287.e: The pancreas releases enzymes into the gut that break down food. It also produces hormones such as insulin, which control blood sugar.
9287.m: The pancreas helps with digestion and blood sugar.

9288.q: How does the weight of male and female chamois usually differ?
a: Males are usually a little heavier
Females are always twice as heavy
9288.e: Male chamois, called bucks, are on average a little heavier and stronger than the females. But the difference is not huge.
9288.m: Chamois bucks are usually a little heavier.

9289.q: How are young lion cubs born?
a: With open eyes and very strong
Already as big as adult lions
9289.e: Lion cubs are born blind and can hardly walk at first. Only after a few days do they open their eyes.
9289.m: Lion cubs are blind at first.

9290.q: When are moose calves usually born?
9290.e: The calves are born in May or June. Then there is plenty of fresh food.

9291.q: What further danger do electricity pylons pose to red kites?
a: Electric shock when landing on unprotected pylons
Too much noise from the electricity
Too much bright light at night
Too much heat under the cables
9291.e: When red kites land on poorly protected pylons, they can get a deadly electric shock. That is why modern pylons are built to be bird-safe.
9291.m: Unprotected pylons are dangerous for red kites.

9292.q: Which insects do trout often catch right from the water surface?
9292.e: Trout sometimes jump or snap at insects flying above the water. These are, for example, small midges or mayflies.
9292.m: Trout snap up insects above the water.

9293.q: What happens to young kestrels after they leave the nest?
a: Their parents keep feeding them for a while
They must survive completely alone at once
They never return near the nest
Their parents chase them away immediately
9293.e: Even after their first flight, young kestrels stay near the nest for some time. The parents keep feeding them until they can hunt on their own.
9293.m: Parents still feed the young after they fledge.

9294.q: What does a housefly do with solid food before eating it?
a: It spits saliva on it to make it liquid
It carries it to a hiding place
It crushes it with its wings
It warms it up in the sun
9294.e: Because the housefly cannot chew, it spits saliva onto solid food. This makes the food soft and liquid, so the fly can suck it up.
9294.m: Saliva turns the food into liquid.

9295.q: Which animal often eats white grubs in the soil?
9295.e: The mole hunts worms and larvae in the soil, including white grubs. It finds them with its senses of touch and smell.

a: No, it can only stand in puddles
No, it would drown at once
9296.e: Least weasels are good swimmers, even if they do not go looking for water. This skill sometimes helps them escape or hunt.

9297.q: How does the close bond of a bearded vulture pair show?
a: They often stay together for life
They split up completely every year
They always live in large groups
They share their territory with many other pairs
9297.e: Bearded vultures often form a stable partnership for many years and use the same territory and the same nest again and again. This helps them raise young successfully.
9297.m: Bearded vulture pairs often stay together for life.

9298.q: How do gibbons mainly move through the trees?
a: They swing from branch to branch with their arms
They jump on all fours like squirrels
They climb slowly using their tail
9298.e: This way of moving is called brachiation. Gibbons have very long arms and strong hands for it.
9298.m: Gibbons swing arm over arm through the trees.

9299.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult male lynx get?
9299.e: Male lynxes are bigger and heavier than females. They reach a weight similar to a large dog.
9299.m: A lynx weighs about as much as a large dog.

9300.q: From which neighbouring country did brown bears start coming back into Switzerland from 2005?
9300.e: In 2005 the bear JJ2 came from Trentino in Italy into the Lower Engadine. It was the first wild bear in Switzerland for about a hundred years.
9300.m: Bears come into Switzerland from Italy.

9301.q: What do newly hatched budgie chicks look like?
9301.e: Budgie chicks hatch naked, blind and completely helpless. Their parents feed them until they can look after themselves.

9302.q: Is there a closed season for pike in some waters?
a: Yes, then they must not be caught
No, they can be caught all year
No, pike may never be caught
9302.e: During the spawning season there is often a closed season for pike. In this time they must not be fished, so that they can breed.
9302.m: A closed season applies during spawning.

9303.q: What are the adult ants called that are neither queens nor males?
9303.e: Workers are adult ants without wings. They do almost all the jobs in the nest.

9304.q: Roughly how much bamboo can an adult panda eat in one day?
a: Several kilograms, often a great deal
Only a little once a week
9304.e: Because bamboo has few nutrients, a panda has to eat huge amounts of it. In one day it often eats many kilograms.
9304.m: Pandas eat a lot of bamboo every day.

9305.q: What shape is the robin’s beak?
a: Thin and pointed, for catching insects
Thick and wide, like a duck’s
9305.e: The thin, pointed beak helps the robin catch small insects and worms. That way it can peck well among the leaves.
9305.m: The beak is thin and pointed.

9306.q: How old does a least weasel usually get in the wild?
9306.e: A least weasel’s life in the wild is short and dangerous. Many fall victim to predators or harsh winters.
9306.m: Least weasels usually live only a short time.

9307.q: What is special about the Alpine salamander’s habitat compared with many other amphibians?
a: It is found especially at high mountain altitudes
It is found only in tropical rainforests
9307.e: While many amphibians live in lower, warmer areas, the Alpine salamander has adapted to the harsh mountain climate. This makes it a special species in Europe.
9307.m: It is adapted to life in the mountains.

9308.q: What job does a sentry have in a meerkat group?
a: It looks out for enemies and warns the others
It is the only one to find food for everyone
It digs the whole burrow alone
9308.e: The sentry sits up high and watches the surroundings. When there is danger, it warns the group with calls.
9308.m: The sentry warns the group of danger.

9310.q: In which well-known desert or region in southern Africa do meerkats live?
9310.e: The Kalahari in southern Africa is a typical meerkat habitat. The Sahara is in the north of Africa.
9310.m: The Kalahari is a meerkat habitat.

9312.q: How can you easily tell a perch from a trout?
a: By its dark vertical stripes and spiny fin
By the red spots on its body
By the long barbels on its mouth
9312.e: The perch has dark vertical bands and a spiny front dorsal fin. The brown trout, on the other hand, can be recognised by its red and black spots.
9312.m: Stripes and spines give the perch away.

9313.q: What purpose do special nest boxes for peregrine falcons on tower blocks or church towers sometimes serve?
a: They provide a safe nesting site instead of natural cliffs
They serve as feeding places for pigeons
They are meant to keep falcons away
9313.e: Special nest boxes replace missing rock ledges and give the falcons a sheltered place for their eggs. This lets them breed successfully in cities too.

9314.q: Which jackal is also found in south-eastern Europe?
9314.e: The golden jackal lives in parts of south-eastern Europe and Asia. Side-striped and black-backed jackals live only in Africa.
9314.m: The golden jackal also lives in Europe.

9315.q: Why does the barn owl often look ghostly at night?
a: Because its pale feathers shimmer in the moonlight
9315.e: The pale, white feathers of the barn owl shimmer almost ghostly in the moonlight. That is why many people used to be frightened of it.

9316.q: From which wild animal is our domestic goat originally descended?
9316.e: The wild bezoar ibex from the Middle East is the ancestor of today’s domestic goats. People tamed it a very long time ago.
9316.m: The bezoar ibex is the original goat.

9317.q: What is one possible reason why marmots live in colonies rather than alone?
a: Together they can warn each other better about enemies
Alone they could run much faster
In groups they no longer find food
Alone they would freeze straight away in summer
9317.e: In a colony there are always several watchful animals that can warn of danger. This clearly raises the chances of survival for all members.
9317.m: Together they are safer from enemies.

9318.q: What is the old town of Solothurn especially known for?
a: Its many old churches and towers
9318.e: Solothurn has a beautiful old town with many old churches, towers and fountains. That is why many tourists like to stroll through its narrow lanes.
9318.m: Solothurn's old town has many churches and towers.

9319.q: How does a small nymph become an adult grasshopper?
a: It moults several times and grows
It forms a pupa like a butterfly
It hatches from an egg in water
It always stays the same small size
9319.e: The nymph sheds its old skin several times. Each time it is a little bigger afterwards.

9320.q: How does an elephant herd usually react when a calf is in danger?
a: All the animals rush to help it
9320.e: Elephants are very caring animals. When a calf is in trouble, several adult elephants from the herd come to help at once.
9320.m: The herd helps calves in danger straight away.

9321.q: What is the name of the order that praying mantises belong to?
9321.e: Mantids have special front legs for catching prey. About 2500 species are known worldwide.

9322.q: Which greenhouse gas is produced, among other things, by keeping livestock and has a particularly strong effect on the climate?
9322.e: Methane is produced, for example, when cows digest their food. Over a short time it affects the climate even more strongly than CO2.
9322.m: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas.

9323.q: In which regions does the wolverine mainly live?
a: In cold northern regions such as Scandinavia and Siberia
Only on small islands in the Pacific
9323.e: The wolverine is found mainly in cold northern areas such as Scandinavia, Siberia and parts of North America. It is well adapted to cold and snow there.
9323.m: The wolverine lives in the cold north.

9324.q: Why is a garden pond helpful for common frogs?
a: It gives them a place to spawn
It serves as their bedroom in summer
It is their only escape from the sun
It is the only place they drink all year
9324.e: A natural garden pond can serve as a spawning site for common frogs in spring. In this way gardeners help frogs survive in built-up areas too.
9324.m: Garden ponds help common frogs spawn.

9325.q: How does a pond skater breathe?
a: Through breathing holes and air tubes
Through its feet in the water
9325.e: Insects have breathing holes on their bodies that lead into air tubes. The pond skater breathes air, even though it lives on the water.
9325.m: It breathes air through breathing holes.

9328.q: What is considered a difference between bonobos and chimpanzees?
a: Bonobos live in trees in the Himalayas
9328.e: Among bonobos, conflicts are less often settled by violence. Chimpanzees more often have fierce fights.
9328.m: Bonobos are considered more peaceful than chimpanzees.

9329.q: How do seahorses eat during the day?
a: They eat small amounts very often
9329.e: Because they have no stomach, seahorses eat small portions again and again throughout the day. That way they get enough energy.

9330.q: What colour is the stoat’s back fur in summer?
9330.e: In summer the stoat has brown fur on its back. This lets it hide well among soil, grass and stones.
9330.m: Summer fur is brown on the back.

9331.q: What effect does climate change have on the snow leopard?
a: Its high mountain habitat is changing
It needs more snow to bathe in
It grows bigger because of it
9331.e: As it gets warmer, the tree line moves higher. This makes its habitat smaller.
9331.m: The climate is changing its habitat.

9332.q: What does a Bactrian camel mainly eat?
a: Plants such as grasses, thorny bushes and salty plants
9332.e: Bactrian camels are herbivores. They also eat tough, thorny and salty plants.
9332.m: Bactrian camels are undemanding plant eaters.

9333.q: What can happen if a dog takes a fire salamander in its mouth?
a: It can cause irritation and, in rare cases, serious poisoning
It has no effect at all on dogs
It makes the dog invisible for ever
9333.e: The poison can cause drooling, trembling or worse symptoms in dogs. So care is needed when dogs are out in the woods.

9334.q: What especially attracts ladybirds to a garden?
a: A compost heap with no plants
9334.e: Where many aphids sit on plants, ladybirds find plenty to eat. That is why gardeners are often happy to welcome these beetles into their gardens.

9335.q: What was the ‘Ostpolitik’ of German Chancellor Willy Brandt?
a: A policy of West Germany drawing closer to East Germany and the Eastern Bloc
A plan to build the Berlin Wall
A military alliance against the Soviet Union
An economic blockade against Eastern Europe
9335.e: From 1969 Willy Brandt sought dialogue with East Germany and other communist states. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for this in 1971.
9335.m: Ostpolitik meant drawing closer to the East.

9336.q: According to research, what can goldfish actually learn?
a: For example, to link certain routes or signals with food
9336.e: Studies show that goldfish can learn and remember, for example, feeding times or routes. So their memory is better than the well-known saying suggests.
9336.m: Goldfish can learn a surprising amount.

9337.q: How long can a queen bee live?
9337.e: Unlike the workers, a queen can live for several years. During this time she lays a great many eggs.
9337.m: Queens live much longer than workers.

9338.q: Apart from nest building, why are reeds important for the great crested grebe?
a: They give cover from enemies and protection for the young
They are its only source of food
They are of no importance at all
9338.e: Reed beds provide not only material for the nest but also important protection from enemies. Young birds in particular find safe hiding places there.

9340.q: What do many goats have on their chin?
9340.e: Many goats, including females, have a small beard on their chin. This is quite normal for these animals.

9341.q: Where does the name “hyena” probably come from?
9341.e: The word comes from the Greek “hýaina”, which is linked to “hys” (pig). The reason was probably the bristly mane.

9342.q: Why is the magpie sometimes wrongly seen as a pest?
a: Because people think it steals many songbird eggs
9342.e: Many believe magpies do great harm to songbirds by eating their eggs and chicks. Studies show, however, that their effect on songbird numbers is small.
9342.m: Magpies harm songbirds less than people think.

9343.q: When does a female brown bear usually give birth to her cubs?
a: During her winter rest in the den
In midsummer out in the open
9343.e: The cubs are usually born in January or February while the mother is still resting in the den. They are tiny at birth and weigh only a few hundred grams.
9343.m: Bear cubs are born in the winter den.

9344.q: What was Anubis responsible for in ancient Egypt?
9344.e: Anubis was seen as the protector god of embalmers. He guided the dead into the underworld.

9345.q: How far can a wolf travel in a single day?
9345.e: Young wolves in particular, looking for a pack of their own, can cover very long distances in a day. This lets them reach new areas far from where they were born.
9345.m: Young wolves often travel very far.

9346.q: Why are the edible frog’s eyes so high up on its head?
a: So it can still see its surroundings while in the water
So it can hunt in total darkness
9346.e: The high eyes let the edible frog stay almost completely under water and still watch its surroundings. Only its eyes and nostrils then stick out of the water.
9346.m: High eyes see above the water.

9347.q: How can experts tell the age of a trout?
a: By the annual rings on its scales
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its snout
9347.e: Rings form on the scales, similar to trees. In winter they grow more slowly, which you can see under a microscope.

9348.q: When do young grey herons usually leave the nest for the first time?
9348.e: Only after about two months can young grey herons fly and leave the nest. Until then their parents feed them.

9349.q: How does a wasp often react if you wave your arms about wildly?
a: It feels threatened and becomes more aggressive
It flies away at once and never comes back
9349.e: Wild waving looks like an attack to the wasp. This can make it feel threatened and more likely to sting.

9350.q: What colour is the chamois’s coat usually in winter?
9350.e: In winter the chamois’s coat becomes darker and thicker. This helps the animal protect itself better from the cold.
9350.m: In winter the chamois coat is dark and thick.

9351.q: In which habitat do bonobos live?
a: In high mountains above the tree line
9351.e: Bonobos live in damp tropical forests, including swamp forests. There they find fruit and trees to sleep in.

9352.q: How can adult kangaroos defend themselves against enemies?
a: They kick hard with their hind legs
9352.e: Kangaroos have very strong hind legs with sharp claws. They can kick forward powerfully with them to defend themselves.

9353.q: What do you measure with an ammeter?
9353.e: An ammeter is put into a circuit to measure how much current flows per second. The unit for this is the ampere.

9354.q: What fur colours do golden hamsters come in?
a: Many, for example golden, white or black
9354.e: Golden hamsters come in many fur colours because they have been bred as pets for a long time. Besides golden, there are white and dark colours.

9355.q: What is true of insects such as the cockchafer when it comes to body temperature?
a: They keep their temperature at 37 degrees
They get a fever in winter
9355.e: Their body temperature depends on their surroundings. When it is cold, insects are sluggish.

9356.q: How is trout à la meunière cooked?
a: Coated in flour and fried in a pan
Baked in the oven with cheese
9356.e: For trout à la meunière, the fish is lightly coated in flour and then fried in a pan. It is a very popular way of cooking trout.
9356.m: Trout à la meunière is fried.

9357.q: In what formation do cranes often fly when migrating?
9357.e: The V formation saves energy because the birds behind fly in the slipstream of those in front. The birds take turns at the front regularly.
9357.m: Cranes fly in an energy-saving V.

9358.q: Where is the wels catfish originally found?
a: In eastern Europe and parts of central Europe
9358.e: Its natural range lies mainly in eastern and central Europe as far as western Asia. It was later released into other countries.
9358.m: It originally lives in eastern and central Europe.

9359.q: Is a sea turtle’s shell flatter or more domed than that of many tortoises?
a: They have no shell at all
9359.e: The shell of sea turtles is flatter than that of tortoises. This helps them move better through the water.
9359.m: Its shell is built flat for swimming.

9361.q: How does the common frog react when it is startled?
9361.e: When in danger, the common frog usually reacts with a quick escape jump. That way it can quickly disappear into thick grass or water.
9361.m: In danger, the common frog jumps away.

9363.q: What particularly threatens bonobos in their homeland?
a: Hunting and the loss of their habitat
Too much competition from polar bears
9363.e: Bonobos are hunted, and the rainforest is being destroyed, for example by logging. Both make their numbers shrink.
9363.m: Hunting and forest loss threaten bonobos.

9364.q: Why do the pond skater’s long legs stay on top of the water?
a: The weight is spread over a large area
9364.e: The animal’s weight is spread over many points of contact. So the water surface is hardly broken.

9365.q: What does the carp use to break up its food?
a: Sharp teeth at the front of its mouth
9365.e: Because the carp has no teeth in its mouth, it breaks up its food with throat teeth deep in its gullet. These grind up hard food.
9365.m: Throat teeth grind the carp’s food.

9366.q: What do some birds and hedgehogs like to do with Roman snails?
9366.e: Birds and hedgehogs are among the natural enemies of the Roman snail. They eat the snails when they find them.

9368.q: Why do children get milk teeth first and permanent teeth later?
a: The jaw grows and later needs bigger teeth
Permanent teeth only grow at night
Milk teeth are made of milk
9368.e: A child's jaw is too small for big teeth. When the jaw grows, stronger permanent teeth come through.
9368.m: Teeth grow along with your jaw.

9369.q: What loud sound does a lion make that can be heard very far away?
9369.e: Lions can roar so loudly that it can be heard several kilometres away. But they cannot purr like a house cat.

9370.q: Which kind of trout lives especially often in large Swiss lakes?
9370.e: The lake trout lives mostly in lakes and only swims into rivers to spawn. In Switzerland it is found in several large lakes.
9370.m: The lake trout mostly lives in lakes.

9371.q: What does a starfish’s skin feel like?
9371.e: The starfish’s skin is rough and covered in many small spines. This protects it from enemies.

9373.q: What is the larva of the cockchafer called?
9373.e: Cockchafer larvae are called white grubs. They live in the soil and eat roots.
9373.m: Cockchafer larvae are called white grubs.

9374.q: Which animal appears on the coat of arms of the city of Bern?
9374.e: According to legend, Bern was named after the first animal killed in the hunt when the city was founded: a bear. Since then the bear has been the city’s symbol.
9374.m: The bear is the symbol of Bern.

9376.q: What is a baby giraffe called?
9376.e: A young giraffe is called a calf, just like a young cow. A giraffe calf is already very big at birth.
9376.m: A baby giraffe is called a calf.

9379.q: Which statement about the sand lizard’s habitat in Switzerland is true?
a: It is found in many cantons but is fairly rare overall and endangered
It is found only in high mountains above 3000 metres
It is the most common reptile in Switzerland
9379.e: Suitable dry and sunny habitats have declined in Switzerland, so the sand lizard is considered endangered. However, it can be found in several regions of the country.
9379.m: In Switzerland it is widespread but endangered.

9380.q: How does the Bactrian camel differ from the dromedary?
9380.e: The Bactrian camel lives mainly in Central Asia and has two humps. The dromedary has only one.
9380.m: Bactrian camel two humps, dromedary one.

9381.q: Why do polar bears not get cold quickly despite the great cold?
a: Because of their thick fur and layer of fat
Because they always stay in warm water
Because their blood is very hot
9381.e: Thick fur and a thick layer of fat protect the polar bear from the cold. That way its body heat is kept in well.
9381.m: Fur and fat protect against the cold.

9382.q: What is the World Economic Forum (WEF), held every year in Switzerland?
a: A meeting of political and business leaders in Davos
9382.e: Every January, important politicians, business leaders and experts from all over the world meet at the WEF in Davos. They discuss global economic and political issues.
9382.m: The WEF takes place every year in Davos.

9383.q: Apart from Switzerland, in which European countries is the common wall lizard found?
a: For example in Italy and France
9383.e: The common wall lizard is widespread in large parts of southern and central Europe, for example in Italy and France. There it finds similar warm habitats.
9383.m: The wall lizard is widespread in southern and central Europe.

9385.q: What does the Alpine salamander mainly feed on?
a: Small invertebrates such as insects and worms
9385.e: The Alpine salamander is a carnivore and catches small insects, spiders, worms and snails. It does not eat plants.

9386.q: What do red deer often do in summer in the Alps?
a: They move up to high mountain meadows
They always stay down in the valley
They migrate to the warm south
9386.e: In summer, red deer often move to higher parts of the mountains. There they find fresh, juicy grass.
9386.m: In summer deer move into the mountains.

9387.q: Why is the kestrel called “Turmfalke” (tower falcon) in German?
a: Because it likes to nest on church towers and tall buildings
Because it only hunts in castle towers
Because its call sounds like a bell tower
Because it always flies in circles around towers
9387.e: The kestrel often nests in niches of church towers, factory chimneys or tower blocks. This liking for tall buildings gave it its German name.
9387.m: Towers are popular nesting sites for the kestrel.

9389.q: How long does a young gorilla usually stay with its mother?
a: Not at all, it lives alone straight away
9389.e: Young gorillas need long care. They often stay with their mother for several years until they are independent enough.
9389.m: Young gorillas stay with their mother for years.

9390.q: When is the ibex rutting season?
9390.e: The ibex rut takes place in winter, usually in December and January. Then the males fight for the favour of the females.

9391.q: Where are lake trout eggs fertilised?
a: In the water outside the body
9391.e: The female lays the eggs, and the male releases milt into the water. So fertilisation happens outside the body.

9392.q: What does a tortoise usually do when it feels threatened?
a: It pulls its head and legs into its shell
It digs itself in within seconds
9392.e: The hard shell is its protection. When in danger, the tortoise pulls its head and legs back under it.
9392.m: In danger, the tortoise hides in its shell.

9393.q: Why are collisions with moose especially dangerous for cars?
a: Because of their great weight and long legs
Because moose always walk in large herds
Because moose attack cars on purpose
Because moose are only out in winter
9393.e: Because of the long legs, the heavy body often hits the windscreen in a crash. This is much more dangerous than with a roe deer.

9394.q: What does the beaver mainly use its broad, flat tail for when swimming?
9394.e: The tail helps the beaver keep its direction in the water and push itself forward. It is also used as an alarm signal when the beaver slaps it loudly on the water.
9394.m: The tail steers the beaver when swimming.

9395.q: How is the barn owl’s body built?
9395.e: The barn owl has a slim body and fairly long wings. This helps it with its calm, quiet gliding flight.

9396.q: In some countries such as France, Roman snails are also eaten. What is this dish often called?
9396.e: In France, Roman snails are considered a delicacy and are called escargots. They are usually prepared with herb butter.
9396.m: Escargot is snail as a dish.

9397.q: Which season is the main breeding season of the mallard?
9397.e: In spring, when it gets warmer and there is more food, the females lay their eggs. This is the best time for raising the ducklings.

9398.q: Roughly how tall is a moose at the shoulder?
9398.e: A moose is about as tall at the shoulder as a tall person. Its long legs make it look very tall.
9398.m: Moose are about two metres tall.

9399.q: What protects a trout’s body like armour?
9399.e: Trout are covered in small, shiny scales. These protect their body in the water.

a: With tracheae, a system of tubes in the body
9400.e: Air enters through small openings on the body, called spiracles, into fine tubes. These carry it to the organs.
9400.m: Insects breathe through fine air tubes.

9401.q: Why is it important that goldfish are not crowded too closely in a tank?
a: Because otherwise there is too little oxygen and too much dirt
Because otherwise they become too colourful
Because otherwise they swim too fast
9401.e: Too many fish in a small space use up a lot of oxygen and quickly make the water dirty. This can harm the animals.
9401.m: Too many fish in a small space is harmful.

9402.q: What can a dromedary do with its nostrils?
a: It can squirt water with them
It can whistle with them like a bird
9402.e: In a sandstorm the animal closes its nostrils. That way less sand gets into its airways.
9402.m: Nostrils can be closed in a storm.

9403.q: What does the tawny owl do with the indigestible remains of its prey, such as bones and fur?
a: It coughs them up again as a pellet
It buries them in the ground
It spits them out right after catching
9403.e: Because the tawny owl often swallows its prey whole, it cannot digest bones, fur and feathers. It presses these remains into a pellet and coughs them up later.
9403.m: The tawny owl coughs up pellets of undigested remains.

9404.q: How old can a wels catfish get?
9404.e: Wels catfish can live to a great age, with reports of over 50 years. They keep growing throughout their lives.
9404.m: Wels catfish live a very long time.

9405.q: What are our domestic cows descended from?
9405.e: Today’s cows are descended from the aurochs, a large wild cattle that no longer exists. People tamed cattle a very long time ago.
9405.m: Cows are descended from the aurochs.

9406.q: How do young tree frogs develop from the eggs?
a: Through tadpoles that develop into frogs in the water
Directly as small frogs with no tadpole stage
9406.e: Tadpoles hatch from the eggs, live in the water and later grow legs. Only then do they change into small frogs.
9406.m: From egg to tadpole to frog.

9407.q: How big can a male lynx’s territory be?
a: Up to several hundred square kilometres
As big as a football pitch
9407.e: Male lynxes need large areas with enough prey. Their territory can overlap with several females’ territories.

9408.q: What do young lake trout in streams mainly eat?
9408.e: Many water insects and their larvae live in streams. They are the right food for small trout.

9409.q: Which animal can change its skin colour to match its surroundings in a flash?
9409.e: The chameleon has special skin cells that let it change colour. This is used for camouflage and for communicating with other chameleons.

9410.q: Where does the female fire salamander give birth to her larvae?
a: In small, cool streams or spring pools
In dry holes in the ground
9410.e: The females release their larvae directly into the water of clean streams. There the larvae can continue to develop.

9412.q: Sadly, why are rhinos often hunted?
9412.e: Poachers hunt rhinos because some people wrongly believe the horn helps against illnesses. But this is not proven and is very bad for the animals.
9412.m: Rhinos are hunted for their horn.

9413.q: What is the pouch called in which seahorse babies grow?
9413.e: The male has a pouch on his belly in which the eggs grow safely. The little seahorses stay in it until they are fully developed.
9413.m: The belly pouch protects the baby seahorses.

9415.q: How do male hippos mark their territory?
a: They spray dung with their tail
9415.e: Male hippos flick dung in all directions with their tail. In this way they mark their area in the water and on land.
9415.m: Hippos mark their territory with dung.

9416.q: Why is the stone marten an important part of nature despite the trouble it causes car owners?
a: It helps to limit the number of mice
It pollinates flowers like a bee
It spreads seeds like a bird
9416.e: Although stone martens sometimes cause trouble, they play an important role in the ecosystem by keeping mouse numbers in check. This shows that even unpopular animals can be useful.
9416.m: Stone martens keep mouse numbers in check.

9417.q: What is the significance of the elephant in Hinduism?
a: The god Ganesha has an elephant’s head
It is seen as a terrifying creature
It is seen as a messenger of death
9417.e: Ganesha is a popular god with an elephant’s head. He stands for wisdom and new beginnings.

9418.q: Which animal family does the stoat belong to?
9418.e: Like the badger and the polecat, the stoat belongs to the weasel family. These animals often have a long body and short legs.
9418.m: The stoat belongs to the weasel family.

9419.q: What great danger from humans threatens elephants the most?
9419.e: Poachers hunt elephants illegally to sell their valuable tusks. This poaching is one of the greatest dangers to elephants.
9419.m: Poaching is a serious threat to elephants.

9420.q: What does “change” mean when you pay?
a: The money you get back when paying
9420.e: If you pay with a larger note, you get the rest back as change. It is worth counting it.
9420.m: Change is what is left over when you pay.

9421.q: What are the young of the mute swan called?
9421.e: The young are called cygnets. They swim with their parents soon after hatching.

9422.q: Which colourful bird dives for small fish, including young trout?
9422.e: The kingfisher sits on a branch by the water and plunges down onto its prey. Its feathers shimmer blue and orange.

9423.q: What is the galaxy that our solar system belongs to called?
9423.e: The Milky Way is a huge galaxy with hundreds of billions of stars, including our sun. On clear nights you can see it as a bright band across the sky.
9423.m: Our solar system lies in the Milky Way.

9424.q: How does alpaca wool compare with sheep’s wool?
a: It is often softer and less itchy
9424.e: Alpaca wool often feels softer and is less itchy. It contains hardly any wool grease and so suits many people well.
9424.m: Alpaca wool is soft and hardly itchy.

9425.q: How are blue whales protected worldwide today?
a: By an international ban on whaling
By locking them up in zoos
By not telling anyone about them
9425.e: Today it is forbidden almost everywhere to hunt blue whales. This is meant to let their numbers recover.

9426.q: Where does a koala usually sleep?
a: In a fork of branches high in a tree
In a burrow under the ground
In a nest of twigs on the ground
9426.e: Koalas spend most of their lives in trees. They often sleep there snuggled into a fork of branches.
9426.m: Koalas sleep high in tree forks.

9427.q: How many young can a mother hamster have in one litter?
9427.e: A mother hamster can give birth to several young at once. Sometimes there are even more than ten.

9429.q: Roughly how old can a grey heron get in the wild?
9429.e: Grey herons can live quite long in the wild, even though many young birds do not survive their first year. Adults sometimes reach two decades.
9429.m: Some grey herons live almost 20 years.

9430.q: How do orangutans in the rainforest often drink?
a: They lick water from tree holes or leaves
They only drink from the sea
They suck up water with a trunk
9430.e: They also get a lot of liquid from fruit. In addition, they use rainwater from leaves or tree hollows.
9430.m: They find water in leaves and fruit.

9433.q: Which danger particularly threatens the Asian elephant?
9433.e: Forests are cleared and turned into fields or settlements. As a result, elephants find less food and come into conflict with people more often.
9433.m: Habitat loss is the greatest danger.

9434.q: How does the stork manage to fly so far without getting tired?
a: it glides on warm rising air
it only ever flies at night
it swims part of the way
9434.e: The stork uses warm rising air currents, called thermals, to climb high and glide without much flapping. This saves a lot of energy.

9435.q: What is the butterfly’s night-active relative called?
9435.e: Moths are close relatives of butterflies. Most of them only fly after dark.

9437.q: How does a male brown bear’s home range usually differ from a female’s?
a: Males have no area of their own
Both have exactly the same size of area
9437.e: Male brown bears usually claim a much larger home range than females. This is partly linked to searching for mates.

9438.q: Why are lions in the wild endangered today?
a: Because their habitat keeps getting smaller
Because they have too many cubs
Because they do not like any food
9438.e: As people use more and more land, lions lose their natural habitat. That is why there are far fewer lions today than in the past.

9439.q: What does the tapir use its trunk for?
9439.e: The tapir uses its trunk to pull bits of plants into its mouth. It also smells very well with it.
9439.m: The trunk grabs food and smells.

9440.q: On which continents does the puma live naturally?
9440.e: The puma has the largest range of any wild land mammal in the Western Hemisphere. It stretches from Canada to the south of South America.
9440.m: Pumas live only in the Americas.

9441.q: What makes the squirrel’s front paws especially skilful?
a: It holds nuts with them like little hands
It can swim with them like flippers
It digs deep tunnels with them
9441.e: With its front paws the squirrel skilfully holds nuts and other food, almost like little hands.
9441.m: The front paws work like little hands.

9443.q: What do leafcutter ants need the pieces of leaf they cut for?
a: They grow fungus on them as food
They build a roof for their nest from them
They eat the leaves themselves straight away
9443.e: Leafcutter ants carry pieces of leaf into the nest. There special fungi grow on them, which they need as food.

9444.q: Which group of birds does the robin belong to?
9444.e: The robin is a small songbird. Like the blackbird and the sparrow, it sings often and a lot.

9445.q: How do geese usually communicate within their group?
a: Only by eye contact without sounds
They do not communicate at all
Only by touching with their wings
9445.e: Geese have different calls for different situations, for example to warn or to keep the group together. This is how they communicate with each other.
9445.m: Geese call differently depending on the situation.

9446.q: How old can a Roman snail get?
a: Several years, sometimes even many years
9446.e: Roman snails can live for several years. In a good environment some live even much longer.

9447.q: How do male earwigs often fight each other?
a: They grab each other with their pincers
They butt each other with their heads
They spray each other with poison
9447.e: When they quarrel, males use their pincers. It is usually about rank or females.

9448.q: Where do the young bearded vultures released in the Alps come from?
a: From eggs taken from wild nests
9448.e: The young birds come from a European breeding network of zoos and breeding centres. In Switzerland the Pro Bartgeier foundation coordinates the releases.
9448.m: Young bearded vultures come from breeding centres.

9449.q: What does the otter use its thick fur for?
a: It keeps a warm layer of air next to the body
9449.e: The thick fur traps air and so keeps the otter warm even in cold water. That is why it has to groom its fur regularly.
9449.m: Thick fur keeps the otter warm.

9450.q: What is the endangered puma population in Florida called?
9450.e: The Florida panther is a highly endangered subspecies of the puma. It is specially protected.
9450.m: The Florida panther is a puma.

9451.q: What is the hunting behaviour called in which the puma silently creeps closer and then strikes?
9451.e: The puma creeps up on its prey and surprises it with a short leap. A long chase is not its style.

9452.q: What can develop if red blood cells do not get enough iron?
9452.e: Without enough iron, red blood cells can carry less oxygen. This is called anaemia and makes you tired and pale.
9452.m: A lack of iron can cause anaemia.

9453.q: What is the slime on the wels catfish’s skin for?
a: It protects the skin from germs and injuries
9453.e: The slime layer works like a protective film. It also helps it glide through the water.
9453.m: Slime is the skin’s protective film.

9454.q: Do sea turtles keep growing their whole lives?
a: No, they only grow in the first year
9454.e: Unlike humans, sea turtles grow slowly throughout their lives. That is why very old animals are often especially large.
9454.m: Sea turtles grow all their lives.

9455.q: Which fish family do whitefish belong to?
9455.e: Whitefish are related to salmon, trout and char. They all belong to the salmonids.
9455.m: Whitefish are relatives of salmon and trout.

9457.q: What is the difference between coins and banknotes?
a: Coins are made of metal and usually worth less, notes are made of a special material and meant for larger amounts
Coins are always worth more than notes
9457.e: Coins are made of metal and usually have smaller values. Notes are made of a special material and are meant for larger amounts. In Switzerland there are coins from 5 rappen to 5 francs.
9457.m: Coins have small values, notes large ones.

9458.q: What is the name of the long-haired guinea pig breed whose very long coat reaches almost to the ground?
9458.e: Peruvian guinea pigs have especially long fur that keeps growing and must be brushed regularly. Some owners even trim it.

9459.q: How do nature conservation organisations in Switzerland also help the tree frog?
a: By protecting ponds and pools and creating new ones
By releasing tree frogs from America
9459.e: To secure the tree frog population, conservation organisations create new spawning waters and look after existing ponds. This is meant to preserve the habitat of this endangered species.
9459.m: New ponds help the tree frog.

9460.q: What does the typical call of a peregrine falcon at its nest sound like?
a: A loud, harsh kek kek kek
9460.e: Peregrine falcons call loudly and harshly, especially when disturbed at the nest, often like kek kek kek. This call serves as a warning signal and for defence.
9460.m: A loud kek warns at the nest.

9461.q: Are stag beetles dangerous to humans?
a: Yes, they sting with a sting
9461.e: Stag beetles are not poisonous and have no sting. Large males can pinch hard, but that is rare.
9461.m: Stag beetles are harmless to humans.

9462.q: Why are many gardeners happy to see ladybirds?
a: Because they pollinate flowers like bees
9462.e: Ladybirds eat the aphids that harm plants. So less poison has to be sprayed against pests.

9463.q: Apart from the Eurasian magpie, are there other kinds of magpie?
a: Yes, for example the Iberian magpie in Spain
No, there is only one species worldwide
No, magpies only exist in Europe
9463.e: Besides the Eurasian magpie there are other species, such as the Iberian magpie, which lives mainly on the Iberian Peninsula. Related magpie species also live in North America.
9463.m: There are several magpie species worldwide.

9464.q: How many different species of sea turtle are there worldwide?
9464.e: Researchers today distinguish seven different species of sea turtle. Each species has its own special features.
9464.m: There are seven sea turtle species.

9465.q: What happens at a book burning?
a: Books with unwanted ideas are burned.
Books are taken to a museum.
9465.e: In some dictatorships books the government did not like were burned in public. The aim was to make unwanted ideas disappear.

9466.q: Roughly how big is a newborn polar bear cub?
a: About as small as a guinea pig
As big as a baby elephant
9466.e: A newborn polar bear cub is tiny and weighs only about half a kilogram. But it grows very quickly.
9466.m: Polar bear cubs are tiny at birth.

9467.q: Roughly how much water does an elephant drink on a hot day?
9467.e: Elephants need a lot of water so they do not dry out. On hot days they drink huge amounts of it.
9467.m: Elephants drink a lot of water.

9468.q: How do males sometimes build up a ranking among themselves in the mating season?
a: They wrestle each other for the best calling spots
9468.e: Around a pond, males compete for the best places to call from. This sometimes leads to small scuffles.
9468.m: Rivals wrestle for the best calling spots.

9469.q: What colour are the carrion crow’s eggs typically?
9469.e: Carrion crow eggs are greenish and patterned with brown spots. This camouflage colour protects them from predators in the nest.
9469.m: Crow eggs are greenish with brown spots.

9470.q: What does the polar bear do in summer when the ice melts?
a: It often has to go hungry for longer
9470.e: Without ice the polar bear finds it harder to hunt seals. So in summer it often has to manage for longer without much food.
9470.m: Polar bears often go hungry in summer.

9471.q: What do young jackals do when they play?
a: They practise behaviour for hunting and ranking
9471.e: By scrapping and chasing, the pups learn important skills. Play prepares them for adult life.

9472.q: Which animal group does the African buffalo belong to?
9472.e: It gives birth to live young and feeds them with milk. This is typical of mammals.

9473.q: How many eggs does a female bearded vulture usually lay per clutch?
9473.e: The female usually lays two eggs, but sometimes only one chick survives. The eggs are laid a few days apart.
9473.m: A female bearded vulture usually lays two eggs per clutch.

9474.q: What does a large number of water lice in a stream often show?
a: The water is heavily loaded with organic material
The water is crystal clear and very clean
9474.e: Water lice cope quite well with polluted water that has little oxygen. That is why they are seen as indicators of rather poorer water quality.

9475.q: What usually happens when a mole comes up to the surface?
a: It is in danger there because it is clumsy
It feels most at home there
9475.e: On the surface the mole moves slowly and clumsily. That is why it only rarely comes out, and briefly, because enemies are a danger there.
9475.m: On the surface the mole is vulnerable.

9476.q: What are chimpanzees especially good at with their thumbs?
9476.e: The chimpanzee’s thumb can touch the other fingers. This lets it grip and hold objects very skilfully.
9476.m: With its thumb the chimpanzee grips skilfully.

9477.q: Is the Roman snail protected in Switzerland?
a: No, it may be collected without limit
No, it is a pest with no protection
9477.e: The Roman snail is protected in Switzerland. You must not simply collect it in large numbers.

9478.q: What job does the orangutan’s fur do in the rainforest?
a: It protects against rain and wet
It serves as camouflage in snow
It keeps mosquitoes away with poison
9478.e: The long hair carries rainwater away. So the skin stays drier.

9479.q: How do young storks in the nest get their food?
a: The parents bring it up into the nest
The young fly off to hunt themselves
The young eat the twigs of the nest
9479.e: Stork parents collect frogs, mice and worms. In the nest they bring the food back up, and the young eat it.
9479.m: Stork parents bring up food for their young.

9480.q: Where does the green sandpiper often nest?
a: In old nests of other birds in trees
On reed islands in the water
9480.e: It usually does not build a nest of its own and uses nests of thrushes or other birds. This is unusual for a wader.
9480.m: Green sandpipers often nest in other birds’ tree nests.

9481.q: What do young European pond turtles mainly need as food?
a: Small water creatures such as insect larvae and water fleas
9481.e: The young hunt prey that suits their size. As they grow, they also eat bigger animals.
9481.m: The young hunt small water creatures.

9482.q: Which part of an elephant’s body is especially sensitive and important for touch?
9482.e: There are many nerve endings at the tip of the trunk. With it an elephant can even pick up small things.
9482.m: The tip of the trunk is very sensitive to touch.

9483.q: What is a baby cat called?
9483.e: Baby cats are called kittens. In the first weeks they cannot see well yet.

9484.q: What does it mean that the grass snake is cold-blooded?
a: Its body temperature depends on its surroundings
It can heat itself like a dog
9484.e: Cold-blooded animals make hardly any heat of their own. That is why the grass snake likes to sunbathe.
9484.m: For the cold-blooded grass snake, the surroundings set the body temperature.

a: An organisation that supports poor countries with development projects
9485.e: The World Bank gives loans and know-how to countries so that they can build schools, roads or hospitals, for example. It works closely with the UN.
9485.m: The World Bank supports poorer countries financially.

9486.q: What body shape does the wels catfish have?
a: Long and stretched with a broad head
Slim like an arrow with a pointed snout
9486.e: The wels catfish has a broad, flat head and a long, stretched body. Its tail is flattened at the sides.

9488.q: Apart from loud crowing, what other sounds can a cockerel make?
9488.e: Cockerels have a whole range of sounds, for example to warn of danger or to point out food. But loud crowing is the best-known call.

9489.q: In which country does the giant panda live in the wild?
